question: A utility operates sanitary sewers in several separate drainage basins. What is the best first basis for deciding which basin gets rehabilitation work first?
correctAnswer: A ranking of the basins by risk, using flow, condition and consequence of failure data
explanation: At system scale, limited funds go furthest when basins are ranked by measured risk. Age or a single complaint alone does not show likelihood or consequence of failure.
options: The age of the oldest pipe in each basin, with no other information considered
A ranking of the basins by risk, using flow, condition and consequence of failure data
The basin that generated the most recent public complaint
The basin closest to the main works yard
optionA: The age of the oldest pipe in each basin, with no other information considered
optionB: A ranking of the basins by risk, using flow, condition and consequence of failure data
optionC: The basin that generated the most recent public complaint
optionD: The basin closest to the main works yard
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: What is the main purpose of maintaining a complete, current inventory of collection system assets?
correctAnswer: To know what assets exist, where they are located and what condition they are in, so work can be planned
explanation: An inventory that links each asset to its location and condition is the foundation for inspection, maintenance and renewal planning.
options: To satisfy auditors without changing how field work is planned
To replace the need for any field inspection of the assets
To know what assets exist, where they are located and what condition they are in, so work can be planned
To record only the assets that were installed in the current year

question: A new subdivision is about to connect to an existing trunk sewer. What should the collection system manager check first?
correctAnswer: Whether the downstream system has enough remaining capacity for the added flow
explanation: Added development adds flow. Checking downstream capacity before connection prevents surcharging and overflows later.
options: Whether the downstream system has enough remaining capacity for the added flow
Whether the subdivision streets have been named yet
Whether the developer prefers a morning or afternoon connection
Whether the trunk sewer was televised when it was first installed
optionA: Whether the downstream system has enough remaining capacity for the added flow
optionB: Whether the subdivision streets have been named yet
optionC: Whether the developer prefers a morning or afternoon connection
optionD: Whether the trunk sewer was televised when it was first installed

question: Which measure best shows whether a large collection system is improving over several years?

explanation: Outcome trends measured the same way over time, and broken down by basin, show whether management actions are actually improving performance.

The number of staff meetings held each month
The total length of new pipe installed, with no outcome data
Trends in overflows, sewer backups and wet weather flows, tracked consistently by basin

explanation: Standard procedures make results comparable between districts and let staff move between areas without retraining on basic methods.

So that every district must buy equipment on the same day each year

Building laterals, foundation drains and roof leaders connected to the sanitary sewer

question: A utility lines a trunk main, but wet weather flows barely change. What is the most likely explanation the program should test next?
correctAnswer: Much of the I&I is entering through the laterals and maintenance holes rather than the lined main itself
explanation: Lining a main seals only that pipe. If flows stay high, connected laterals and maintenance holes are the likely remaining entry points.
options: The lining material expanded and reduced the pipe diameter
The flow meters were installed in the wrong time zone
Residents increased their water use because the main was lined
Much of the I&I is entering through the laterals and maintenance holes rather than the lined main itself
optionA: The lining material expanded and reduced the pipe diameter
optionB: The flow meters were installed in the wrong time zone
optionC: Residents increased their water use because the main was lined
optionD: Much of the I&I is entering through the laterals and maintenance holes rather than the lined main itself
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

More metres of pipe were lined this year than last year
Fewer staff hours were charged to the basin this year
The basin received a new name in the asset registry

question: In rainfall derived inflow and infiltration analysis, the three response components are usually described by their timing. What do they represent?
correctAnswer: A fast inflow response, a medium response and a slow infiltration response after rainfall
explanation: RDII is separated into fast, medium and slow components because direct inflow, delayed inflow and groundwater infiltration respond on different time scales.
options: Flow from three different treatment plants arriving at one trunk
A fast inflow response, a medium response and a slow infiltration response after rainfall
Morning, afternoon and overnight sanitary flows on a dry day
Flows measured at the start, middle and end of a pipe reach
optionA: Flow from three different treatment plants arriving at one trunk
optionB: A fast inflow response, a medium response and a slow infiltration response after rainfall
optionC: Morning, afternoon and overnight sanitary flows on a dry day
optionD: Flows measured at the start, middle and end of a pipe reach

correctAnswer: By subtracting the dry weather flow pattern, including groundwater base flow, from the wet weather record
explanation: The wet weather record contains normal sanitary flow plus RDII. Removing the dry weather baseline leaves the rainfall derived portion.
options: By subtracting the largest hourly flow from the smallest hourly flow
By dividing the wet weather flow by the number of rain gauges
By removing all flow recorded during daylight hours
By subtracting the dry weather flow pattern, including groundwater base flow, from the wet weather record

optionB: By dividing the wet weather flow by the number of rain gauges
optionC: By removing all flow recorded during daylight hours
optionD: By subtracting the dry weather flow pattern, including groundwater base flow, from the wet weather record

Sub-basin A receives more rainfall than sub-basin B in every storm
Sub-basin A has larger diameter pipes than sub-basin B
Sub-basin B has no sanitary sewer connections

optionB: Sub-basin A receives more rainfall than sub-basin B in every storm
optionC: Sub-basin A has larger diameter pipes than sub-basin B
optionD: Sub-basin B has no sanitary sewer connections

question: Wet weather flow in a basin stays elevated for several days after rain ends, long after surface runoff has stopped. What source does this pattern most suggest?
correctAnswer: Groundwater infiltration through defects below the water table
explanation: A slow, long recession is the signature of groundwater entering through submerged defects, rather than direct surface inflow, which drains quickly.

Groundwater infiltration through defects below the water table
A cross connection from a storm sewer at a single inlet
A pump station discharging on a fixed timer
optionA: Roof leaders discharging directly to the sanitary sewer
optionB: Groundwater infiltration through defects below the water table
optionC: A cross connection from a storm sewer at a single inlet
optionD: A pump station discharging on a fixed timer

question: For a critical lift station, what does firm pumping capacity mean?
correctAnswer: The station can still pump its design peak flow with the largest pump out of service
explanation: Firm capacity is based on the largest unit being unavailable. The remaining pumps must still handle the design peak flow.
options: The station can still pump its design peak flow with the largest pump out of service
The station can run for one hour with no power supply
The station uses only pumps from a single manufacturer
The station can pump its average flow with all pumps running

optionB: The station can run for one hour with no power supply
optionC: The station uses only pumps from a single manufacturer

The flow into the station has stopped completely
The run hour meter needs a new battery and nothing else is wrong

question: Why are air release and vacuum valves installed at high points on a wastewater force main?
correctAnswer: To release accumulated air and admit air when needed, so air binding does not reduce capacity or damage the pipe
explanation: Air collects at high points and can restrict flow and worsen pressure transients. Properly maintained valves at those points protect capacity and the pipe.
options: To add oxygen to the sewage so it stays fresh
To release accumulated air and admit air when needed, so air binding does not reduce capacity or damage the pipe
To measure the flow rate in the force main
To allow crews to enter the force main for inspection
optionA: To add oxygen to the sewage so it stays fresh
optionB: To release accumulated air and admit air when needed, so air binding does not reduce capacity or damage the pipe
optionC: To measure the flow rate in the force main
optionD: To allow crews to enter the force main for inspection
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

correctAnswer: A sudden pump stop or rapid valve closure that abruptly changes the velocity of the moving sewage
explanation: Surge pressures come from sudden velocity changes. Pump trips and fast valve closures are the events a reliability program analyzes and controls.
options: A sudden pump stop or rapid valve closure that abruptly changes the velocity of the moving sewage
A slow seasonal change in sewage temperature
A gradual increase in flow over several weeks
The routine reading of a pressure gauge
optionA: A sudden pump stop or rapid valve closure that abruptly changes the velocity of the moving sewage
optionB: A slow seasonal change in sewage temperature
optionC: A gradual increase in flow over several weeks
optionD: The routine reading of a pressure gauge

question: Why is condition assessment of a force main harder than assessment of a gravity sewer, and what does a reliability program use instead?
correctAnswer: The pipe is pressurized and cannot be taken out of service easily, so the program relies on pressure monitoring, flow data, failure history and targeted inspection technologies
explanation: A pressurized force main cannot simply be opened and televised. Programs combine operating data, transient records and specialized inspection to judge condition.
options: The pipe is always empty, so crews rely only on visual checks from the surface
The pipe is made of a material that cannot be recorded in an inventory
The pipe is pressurized and cannot be taken out of service easily, so the program relies on pressure monitoring, flow data, failure history and targeted inspection technologies
Gravity sewers are also pressurized, so the same camera methods apply directly
optionA: The pipe is always empty, so crews rely only on visual checks from the surface
optionB: The pipe is made of a material that cannot be recorded in an inventory
optionC: The pipe is pressurized and cannot be taken out of service easily, so the program relies on pressure monitoring, flow data, failure history and targeted inspection technologies
optionD: Gravity sewers are also pressurized, so the same camera methods apply directly
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: How do well placed isolation valves and access points improve force main reliability?
correctAnswer: They let crews isolate a damaged section quickly, limiting the volume released and shortening the repair
explanation: Isolation and access do not prevent failures, but they sharply reduce the consequences by limiting spill volume and repair time.
options: They increase the pumping rate of the lift station
They let crews isolate a damaged section quickly, limiting the volume released and shortening the repair
They remove the need for an emergency response plan
They prevent any leak from ever occurring in the main
optionA: They increase the pumping rate of the lift station
optionB: They let crews isolate a damaged section quickly, limiting the volume released and shortening the repair
optionC: They remove the need for an emergency response plan
optionD: They prevent any leak from ever occurring in the main

question: At which location on a force main system is internal corrosion from hydrogen sulfide usually most severe?
correctAnswer: At air pockets and at the discharge point, where hydrogen sulfide is released from the sewage and can form acid on exposed surfaces
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide causes the most damage where it leaves solution and contacts moist exposed surfaces, such as air pockets and the discharge structure.
options: At the lowest point of the main, fully submerged at all times
Inside the pump volute, where the sewage is moving fastest
On the outside of buried pipe that has a protective coating and no damage
At air pockets and at the discharge point, where hydrogen sulfide is released from the sewage and can form acid on exposed surfaces
optionA: At the lowest point of the main, fully submerged at all times
optionB: Inside the pump volute, where the sewage is moving fastest
optionC: On the outside of buried pipe that has a protective coating and no damage
optionD: At air pockets and at the discharge point, where hydrogen sulfide is released from the sewage and can form acid on exposed surfaces
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

question: A long force main discharges into a gravity trunk, and severe corrosion is found in the trunk just downstream of the discharge. What chain of events best explains the damage?
correctAnswer: Long detention in the force main made the sewage septic and generated sulfide, which was released as hydrogen sulfide at the turbulent discharge and formed acid on the trunk's exposed surfaces
explanation: Detention in a full force main produces sulfide. Turbulence at discharge strips hydrogen sulfide into the air space, where it converts to acid and attacks concrete and metal.
options: Long detention in the force main made the sewage septic and generated sulfide, which was released as hydrogen sulfide at the turbulent discharge and formed acid on the trunk's exposed surfaces
The trunk was built downstream of the discharge, so its position alone caused the damage
Chlorine added at the treatment plant travelled backward into the trunk
Cold winter air entered the trunk and froze the pipe wall from inside
optionA: Long detention in the force main made the sewage septic and generated sulfide, which was released as hydrogen sulfide at the turbulent discharge and formed acid on the trunk's exposed surfaces
optionB: The trunk was built downstream of the discharge, so its position alone caused the damage

question: A utility is choosing a chemical dosing approach for sulfide control in a rising main. Which basis for the decision is most defensible?

The dosing rate used by a neighbouring utility on a main of a different length
Measured sulfide levels, detention time and flow in that main, checked by trial dosing and downstream monitoring of results
A fixed dose applied year round with no monitoring of sulfide

It must seal the wet well completely so no air can ever be exchanged
It must vent untreated air at ground level toward the nearest homes

question: With limited inspection funds, which structures should a corrosion program inspect first?
correctAnswer: Structures downstream of force main discharges and other turbulent points where hydrogen sulfide is released, with a history or signs of attack
explanation: Corrosion risk concentrates where hydrogen sulfide leaves solution and attacks exposed surfaces. History and location together set inspection priority.

Newly installed structures that have never carried flow
Structures chosen at random so that every area is treated the same

optionD: Structures chosen at random so that every area is treated the same

By whether the chemical supplier reports good sales in the area

question: What is the central strategy of an effective fats, oils and grease program?

Diluting grease by encouraging establishments to run more hot water

Waiting for blockages and then billing the nearest restaurant
